label: Senior backend / platform engineer — English technical screen

context.resume:
Dana Okonkwo — software engineer, fifteen years, split between embedded systems and backend services.

Meridian Controls (2022-present) — engineering lead. Industrial telemetry for food processing plants. Owns the technology choices across firmware and cloud. Firmware for flow metering, temperature logging and load-cell weighing on ESP32 and STM32. Built the ingest service that collects from about four hundred devices in the field. C, Python, Modbus TCP, MQTT, Docker, PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB.

Arbor Systems (2018-2022) — senior backend engineer, then tech lead. Multi-tenant SaaS for equipment rental. Teams of three to six engineers per project. Replaced a fourteen-year-old pricing engine on a staged cutover rather than a rewrite: ran both engines in parallel against live traffic for six weeks, compared outputs nightly, and switched over when the residual difference held under 0.05%. Built the tenant isolation layer and the reporting pipeline. Python, Django, Django REST Framework, Vue 3, PostgreSQL, Docker, AWS.

Northfield Instruments (2014-2018) — software developer. Data acquisition and visualization for environmental monitoring stations. Wrote the parser library for the vendor's binary format and the web viewer that replaced a desktop client. Both still in production nine years later.

Teaching: adjunct lecturer in embedded systems at the state polytechnic since 2016, roughly thirty students a year. Courses on real-time control, PLC programming and FPGA design in VHDL.

MSc in Electrical Engineering (2011). BSc in Electrical Engineering with distinction (2009).

Open source: Lantern, a vendor-neutral toolchain for industrial sensor data — binary format parsers, a normalization layer, a time-series store adapter and a browser viewer.

Skills: Python, C, VHDL, Django, Django REST Framework, Vue 3, ESP32, STM32, Modbus TCP, MQTT, Docker and Docker Swarm, PostgreSQL, TimescaleDB, AWS. Real-time control, signal processing, distributed systems, time-series modelling.

Based in Lisbon. Works in English and Portuguese.
context.role: Senior Backend Engineer, Platform team. Python and Django services behind a multi-tenant SaaS, Postgres, Docker, AWS. The team owns billing, an internal API used by three product squads, and the data pipeline that feeds reporting. They are explicitly looking for someone who has replaced a legacy system without a big-bang rewrite, who is comfortable owning a cutover, and who can mentor two junior engineers. Interview is a 45-minute technical screen with the team lead: system design discussion, some questions on Postgres behaviour under load, and a short code reading exercise.
context.notes: Lead on the call is the person who wrote the original billing service. Do not frame the pricing-engine work as 'replacing bad code' — frame it as a cutover with a measurable error budget. They asked twice in the recruiter screen about mentoring, so it matters more than the job post suggests. Open question to ask them: what does on-call actually look like for the platform team.
